name: World Stats
author: yakuda
description: Three things your chatbox line usually wants and VRChat does not send over OSC. Instance info: how many players are around you, the world name and the access type, read from VRChat's output_log - Steam/Proton prefix on Linux, AppData\\LocalLow on Windows - with no extra tools. Two session counters: how long you have been in the current instance and how long you have been in VR this session, both taken from the log's own timestamps so they keep counting when the chatbox is restarted mid-session. A clock that stands on its own: it has no connection to the log watcher and keeps running when VRChat is closed or the whole instance half is switched off, with an optional date, weekday and a second time zone for friends abroad. And your headset battery, read either over adb from the headset itself - Quest, Pico, Vive Focus, no matter whether you stream with WiVRn, ALVR or nothing at all - over the running OpenXR runtime itself (WiVRn/Monado, through libmonado - no adb setup, headset plus controllers plus trackers), or over SteamVR/OpenVR. Every part can be used without the other two.
summary: Players, world and instance type, a standalone clock, and headset/controller battery.

placeholders.player_in_world: number of players in the instance
placeholders.world_time: how long you have been in this instance
placeholders.vr_time: how long VRChat has been running
placeholders.realtime_alt: the clock in a second time zone

settings.label: Player icon
settings.hint: Prefix in front of the player count, empty for none

settings.label: World name length
settings.hint: Longer names are cut off - the chatbox has limited space

settings.label: Session time
settings.hint: Both counters are read out of the log's own timestamps, not measured with a stopwatch started here - restart the chatbox in the middle of a session and they carry on where they were instead of jumping back to zero.

items.label: Time in this world  –  {world_time}
items.hint: Counts from the moment you joined the instance and resets when you leave. Empty while you are not in a world.

items.label: Time in VR  –  {vr_time}
items.hint: The long one: how far into this session you are, across every world you have been through.

items.label: Counted from
items.hint: VRChat is the honest answer to "how long have I been in VR" - it is the first line of the current log file, so it survives an app restart. The other one is a plain stopwatch and only matches your session if you started the chatbox first.

items.label: Only show after
items.hint: Below this the placeholder stays empty instead of announcing that you have been here for zero minutes. Set it to 0 to always show it.

settings.label: Clock
settings.hint: Completely independent of the two rows above. The clock needs no log file, no VRChat and no headset - switch players and world name off and this keeps running on its own.

items.label: Clock format
items.hint: strftime, e.g. %H:%M (21:45) or %I:%M %p (09:45 PM)

items.label: Time zone
items.hint: An IANA name like Europe/Berlin or America/New_York. Leave empty to follow the system clock. On Windows this needs the tzdata package; if a zone cannot be loaded the plugin falls back to local time and says so in the log.

items.label: Date format
items.hint: strftime again, e.g. %d.%m. (24.08.) or %b %d (Aug 24)

items.label: Second time zone  –  {realtime_alt}
items.hint: A second clock next to yours - handy when the people you talk to are in another country.

items.label: Second zone
items.hint: IANA name, same as above

items.label: Second zone prefix
items.hint: Written in front of the second clock, empty for none

settings.label: Headset battery
settings.hint: Also independent of the rest - it works outside a world and outside VRChat.

items.label: Battery  –  {hmd_battery}
items.hint: Off means off: no adb process and no OpenVR session are kept alive while this is unchecked.

items.label: Status
items.hint: Written by the plugin - which backend answered, which headset, and what it reads.

items.label: Read the battery once, now
items.hint: Skips the wait for the next poll. The answer lands in the Status row above.

items.label: Where to read it from
items.hint: Auto asks the OpenXR runtime first, then SteamVR, then adb. On WiVRn the runtime already knows the headset charge, so pinning it to WiVRn/Monado saves the other two probes; pin it to adb only if you run no Linux runtime at all.

items.label: Read every
items.hint: A battery moves by one percent every few minutes, so there is nothing to gain below a minute - and adb costs a process each time.

items.label: Only show below
items.hint: Leave at 100 to always show it. Lower it and the placeholder stays empty while the headset is still full - the chatbox gets those characters back for something worth saying.

items.label: Charging icon
items.hint: Replaces the icon above while the headset is on the cable, empty to keep the same icon either way

items.label: Controllers and trackers too  –  {controller_battery} {tracker_battery}
items.hint: WiVRn/Monado and SteamVR only. Android knows nothing about the controllers, so this stays empty on the adb backend.

items.label: Tracker icon
items.hint: The tracker placeholder shows the emptiest tracker, not all of them - that is the one you want to know about.

items.label: WiVRn / Monado  –  the OpenXR runtime
items.hint: Reads libmonado, the same library WayVR and Monado's own tools use. Nothing to install and nothing to configure: the library is found through the active_runtime.json of whichever runtime is currently active. It answers only while a session is running, and it never starts one. The library is loaded in a short-lived helper process, not in the app - if it crashes or hangs, this backend goes quiet for 30 seconds and the chatbox carries on.

items.label: libmonado
items.hint: Written by the plugin: where libmonado was found, or why it was not.

items.label: adb  –  standalone headsets
items.hint: Quest, Pico, Vive Focus and friends. The headset has to be attached over USB or over the network, and you have to accept the USB debugging prompt inside the headset once.

items.label: adb binary
items.hint: Only needed when adb is not on PATH. On Arch it comes with android-tools, on Fedora with android-tools, on Debian with adb.

items.label: Device serial
items.hint: Only matters with more than one device attached - a phone counts. The panel below lists the serials.

items.label: Wireless address
items.hint: For reading the battery over WiFi instead of the cable. Enable wireless debugging in the headset first; port 5555 is assumed when you leave it off.

items.label: Connect to that address
items.hint: Runs adb connect once. It stays connected until the headset reboots or leaves the network.

items.label: SteamVR  –  controllers, trackers, wired headsets
items.hint: Reads SteamVR's own device list. The plugin attaches as a background application, which never starts SteamVR by itself - while SteamVR is closed this backend simply reports nothing.

items.label: Install the openvr package
items.hint: pip install openvr into the interpreter the app runs on. Needs an app restart afterwards. Skip this entirely if you only use the adb backend.

settings.label: VRChat log folder
settings.hint: Leave empty for auto-detect - Steam/Proton prefix on Linux, AppData\\LocalLow on Windows. Only the players/world rows use this; clock and battery do not touch it.
